WallGraphics - licences and attribution (prepared October 14, 2026, revised October 15, 2026)
=============================================================================================

Three groups of content. Per-file SHA-256 hashes, source URLs and commits are in sources.json.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Artwork/Art_*.jpg - public-domain paintings (9 files)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Source repository : https://github.com/pmilovanov/hermitage-art
Commit            : b8ead49c010eac0c8366bafc4ffaaf1f1a447805 (2021-01-28)
Repository licence: CC0 1.0 Universal (LICENSE file in the repository; repository
                    description: "High-res images of paintings from the Hermitage museum
                    (public domain)"). The file names match the Wikimedia Commons
                    "Google Art Project" scans of these paintings.
Status            : Public domain. Every painter died in or before 1926 (eight of the nine
                    before 1910), so the paintings are out of copyright under life + 70
                    terms (EU, UK, Russia, US for unpublished works) and under US
                    publication rules. Monet (d. 1926) is the only one whose life + 100
                    term, used in a few countries such as Mexico, runs to 1 January 2027. The images are faithful photographic
                    reproductions of two-dimensional works, which carry no new copyright
                    in the US (Bridgeman v. Corel, 1999) or the EU (Directive 2019/790,
                    article 14). The repository owner additionally dedicates the files to
                    CC0 1.0. No attribution is required; it is given here as courtesy.
Licence URLs      : https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
                    https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/

  File                                    Painting (artist, life)
  Art_FantinLatour_RosesAndNasturtiums    Roses and Nasturtiums in a Vase, 1883 - Henri Fantin-Latour (1836-1904)
  Art_Heda_BreakfastWithLobster           Breakfast with a Lobster, 1648 - Willem Claesz Heda (1594-1680)
  Art_Pereda_StillLifeEbonyChest          Still Life with an Ebony Chest, 1652 - Antonio de Pereda (1611-1678)
  Art_Pissarro_BoulevardMontmartre        Boulevard Montmartre in Paris, 1897 - Camille Pissarro (1830-1903)
  Art_Monet_WaterlooBridgeFog             Waterloo Bridge, Effect of Fog, 1903 - Claude Monet (1840-1926)
  Art_Lorrain_MorningInTheHarbour         Morning in the Harbour, c.1640s - Claude Lorrain (c.1600-1682)
  Art_Aivazovsky_NinthWave                The Ninth Wave, 1850 - Ivan Aivazovsky (1817-1900)
  Art_Bellotto_NeumarktDresden            The Neumarkt in Dresden, c.1747 - Bernardo Bellotto (1722-1780)
  Art_Robert_LandscapeWithWaterfall       Landscape with a Waterfall, 1802 - Hubert Robert (1733-1808)

Changes: scan border / colour bar cropped, CMYK files converted to sRGB through their
embedded ICC profile, resized to 2048 px on the long side (sides multiples of 4), light
unsharp mask, saved as JPEG quality 86. No other alteration.
Also used (not shipped as a separate file): Claude Monet, "Poppy Field" (same repository and
commit, public domain) as the picture of Store/Calendar_October2026.png.
No identifiable living people: the subjects are still lifes, landscapes, sea and street
scenes painted between 1640 and 1903.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Everything else - project-owned original artwork
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Artwork/FrameMoulding_Gilt_Color.jpg, Artwork/FrameMoulding_Gilt_Normal.png, Brand/*,
Store/*, Street/* were created for Jewelry-store-vr-demo on October 14, 2026 with Python
(numpy, scipy, Pillow). Generator scripts: Source~/ (Unity ignores folders ending in "~").
The jewellery in the posters is rendered by the project's own small ray tracer
(Source~/jrt.py: procedural studio lighting, analytic brilliant-cut gems, signed-distance
metal); no photographs, HDRIs or third-party 3D models are in those images.
Licence: project-owned; may be used, changed and redistributed with the project without
restriction. No third-party attribution is needed.

Fonts: glyphs were rendered into the images from font files in https://github.com/google/fonts
(commit e9678a5385322c63730122ba464765baad83cfd8). No font file is shipped in this pack.
SIL Open Font License 1.1 (https://openfontlicense.org): Barlow, Cinzel, Cormorant Garamond, Tenor Sans, Libre Baskerville, Caveat, Great Vibes,
Pinyon Script, Roboto Condensed, Anton, Bebas Neue, Oswald, Old Standard TT, PT Serif,
UnifrakturMaguntia, Sedgwick Ave Display.
Apache License 2.0 (https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0): Homemade Apple, Permanent
Marker, Rock Salt.
Both licences allow text set in the fonts to be used in images without restriction.

Fictional content: "Aurel & Finch" (shop), "Corvane Alarm Systems", "Ashcombe & Vey
Underwriting", "Northbridge School of Gemmology", "Marrowby Bullion & Findings",
"Quellbrook Glazing", "The Evening Lamplighter", every person's name (Eleanor M. Finch,
Marcus, Priya, Tom, Grace, H. J. Calloway, R. M. Osei, Mabel the cat) and every event on the
street posters are invented. Web searches on October 14, 2026 found no business trading
under the shop, alarm or underwriter names. Web searches on October 15, 2026 found nothing
named "Quellbrook Glazing" or "Quellbrook", "Northbridge School of Gemmology", or "Marrowby"
in bullion or jewellery, and no newspaper called "The Evening Lamplighter" (the nearest is
an unrelated weekly, the La Mirada Lamplighter in California). Telephone numbers use
Ofcom's ranges reserved for drama (020 7946 0xxx, 07700 900xxx, 0161 496 0xxx). Payment cards
on the sticker are generic shapes with no scheme logos; no real police force crest, insignia
or reference number is shown; the "no parking" disc follows the generic Vienna Convention
pattern.

Correction (October 15, 2026): the glazier's business card on Store/NoticeBoard_StaffCork.jpg
first read "Clearview Glazing". That is the name of real UK businesses (for example Clearview
Glazing Ltd, Companies House 03401763), so it was wrongly listed here as invented. The card
now reads "Quellbrook Glazing" and the image was rebuilt from Source~/store_b.py.
